title: SanDisk Drops 9% After Earnings Beat, Guidance Boost & 8‑for‑1 Split; WD, Seagate, Micron Slide
body:
SanDisk Corp. (NASDAQ: SNDK) saw its stock tumble 9% on Thursday despite reporting earnings that beat analysts’ expectations, announcing a $3 billion share‑repurchase program and unveiling an 8‑for‑1 stock split. The sharp decline rippled through the broader memory‑chip sector, pulling Western Digital (WDC) down 8%, Seagate Technology (STX) off 7% and Micron Technology (MU) sliding 6% in a single trading session. Investors appeared to be spooked by a combination of macro‑economic headwinds, pricing pressures and a lingering concern that the company’s recent rally may have run out of steam.

The earnings release showed SanDisk posting revenue of $2.46 billion for the quarter, up 12% year‑over‑year, and an adjusted earnings per share of $1.87, comfortably above the consensus estimate of $1.71. Management highlighted robust demand for solid‑state drives (SSDs) in data‑center and consumer‑grade laptops, as well as a record‑high gross margin of 46.2%. To reward shareholders, the board approved a $3 billion buyback, the largest in the company’s history, and declared a 3% dividend increase. The 8‑for‑1 split, slated for early 2025, was positioned as a way to make the shares more accessible to retail investors.

Yet the market reaction suggested that the positive numbers were not enough to offset broader concerns. Analysts pointed to a slowdown in the PC market, which has been a key driver of SanDisk’s growth, and a tightening of corporate IT budgets amid lingering inflationary pressures. “The earnings beat is nice, but the guidance for the next quarter is modest, and the macro backdrop remains uncertain,” said Daniele Russo, an equity analyst at Meridian Capital. “Investors are pricing in a potential slowdown in data‑center spend, which could blunt demand for high‑end NAND flash.”

The sector‑wide sell‑off also reflected lingering supply‑chain anxieties. Over the past six months, memory manufacturers have been grappling with a glut of NAND chips, leading to price volatility that erodes profit margins. While SanDisk managed to sustain a healthy margin this quarter, analysts warned that the company’s ability to maintain such performance could be tested if inventory levels rise or if competitors launch newer, higher‑density products at lower cost. “The memory market is cyclical by nature,” noted Karen Liu, senior market strategist at Global Insights. “Even a company with a strong balance sheet like SanDisk can see its stock punished when investors anticipate a trough in the cycle.”

The reaction also highlighted a shift in investor sentiment toward growth‑oriented tech names after a year of rallying sharply. SanDisk’s stock had surged more than 70% since the start of 2024, making it one of the year’s standout performers. Some traders may have taken profits, especially after the company’s announcement of the split, which can attract speculative buying but also prompts short‑term repositioning. Moreover, the massive buyback, while signaling confidence, can be interpreted as a defensive move to prop up a stock that may be overvalued relative to its peers.

Looking ahead, SanDisk’s management remains optimistic, forecasting a 5% to 7% revenue growth for the next quarter and promising continued investment in next‑generation 3D NAND technology. The company also plans to expand its footprint in emerging markets, where demand for affordable SSDs is rising. However, the immediate market reaction underscores the delicate balance between strong quarterly results and the broader macro environment that can quickly reshape investor expectations.

In the coming weeks, market participants will be watching closely for any signs that the pricing pressure on NAND chips eases, as well as for updates on corporate‑IT spending trends. If SanDisk can sustain its margin expansion and deliver on its growth roadmap, the recent dip may prove to be a temporary correction. Conversely, a prolonged slowdown in PC and data‑center demand could keep the memory sector under pressure, potentially prompting further volatility in the stocks of SanDisk’s peers.
